scene-dark.note: Store Mode camera backdrop, not used in light-scheme UI chrome.

lamp-room-tag.note: The one Lamplight surface that isn't a straight brown/cream swap of its light counterpart (white).

display.purpose: Screen titles, verdict headline, cover-art titles, stamp copy. Never body or UI chrome.

black.purpose: Primary button/chip-selected labels, verdict card title, vertical spine titles, pocket-card values.

heavy.purpose: Chip labels, LeaderRow emphasis, status lines.

hand.purpose: TapeNote only — never a control. Dewey's speech bubble uses Bold, not Hand.

shadows.name: raised-default
shadows.value: solid offset layer, 3px right/down, color = scheme line, radius matches host
shadows.purpose: Default hard shadow: pocket cards, buttons, bubbles, toasts, stamp host card.

shadows.name: raised-bookcase
shadows.purpose: The bookcase panel — pushed slightly harder than the default to mark it as the screen's main object.

shadows.name: raised-back-button
shadows.purpose: Book detail's circular back control — the smallest offset in the system.

shadows.name: raised-pulled-cover
shadows.purpose: Book detail's tilted (-4deg) cover art — the largest offset, the 'pulled off the shelf' moment.

motion.name: routine
motion.purpose: Spine release, bubble ZoomIn, exits generally (~65% of entrance durations).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for all timing-based motion.

motion.name: pop-spring
motion.purpose: The system's only bounce: Dewey's pop-in and the Sticker's slap-on.

motion.name: stamp-slam
motion.purpose: The verdict stamp slamming down; fires a heavy haptic + 3px card shake on impact.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Yellow, the only legal non-Store-Mode use of bus yellow. Face sinks 3px into its own drawn shadow on press.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { position: relative; height: 52px; padding: 0 18px; border-radius: 14px; border: 2.5px solid #2B1D14; background: #F4B41A; color: #2B1D14; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 15px; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #2B1D14; transition: transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.02); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translate(3px, 3px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 #2B1D14; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #2F6FB0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: White secondary button, same outline/shadow language as primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { position: relative; height: 52px; padding: 0 18px; border-radius: 14px; border: 2.5px solid #2B1D14; background: #FFFFFF; color: #2B1D14; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 15px; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #2B1D14; transition: transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: translate(3px, 3px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 #2B1D14; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #2F6FB0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Full-pill room/status chip. Selected = brown fill / white text; unselected = white fill / brown text.
components.css: .ds-chip-row { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-chip { height: 32px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: 999px; border: 2px solid #2B1D14; background: #FFFFFF; color: #2B1D14; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 12.5px; } .ds-chip--selected { background: #2B1D14; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-chip:hover { filter: brightness(0.97); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #2F6FB0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Pocket Card
components.description: White card with a tomato top rule and dotted-leader rows. Replaces stat-grid layouts system-wide.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-pocket-card { position: relative; border-radius: 8px; border: 2.5px solid #2B1D14; background: #FFFFFF; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #2B1D14; overflow: hidden; } .ds-pocket-card__rule { height: 9px; background: #E2462B; border-bottom: 2px solid #2B1D14; } .ds-pocket-card__body { padding: 8px 14px; } .ds-pocket-card__title { font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.4px; color: #6B5646; margin-bottom: 2px; } .ds-leader-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 0; font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; color: #2B1D14; } .ds-leader-row__dots { flex: 1; border-bottom: 2px dotted #6B5646; margin-bottom: 4px; }

components.name: Stamp
components.description: Rubber-stamp verdict copy (ALREADY YOURS). Slams onto the verdict card with a heavy haptic and a card shake at impact.
components.css: .ds-stamp { display: inline-block; border: 2.5px solid #E2462B; background: #FFFFFF; border-radius: 6px; padding: 3px 10px; transform: rotate(-9deg); font-family: 'Bagel Fat One', serif; font-size: 19px; color: #E2462B; }

components.name: Sticker
components.description: Round yellow 'NEW!' sticker that spring-slaps onto the verdict card on a new find.
components.css: .ds-sticker { width: 62px; height: 62px; border-radius: 50%; background: #F4B41A; border: 2.5px solid #2B1D14; box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #2B1D14; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; transform: rotate(14deg); font-family: 'Bagel Fat One', serif; font-size: 16px; color: #2B1D14; text-align: center; }

components.name: Spine
components.description: Signature component: an outlined book spine whose color/size/pattern is deterministic from the copy's id, so a copy always renders the same spine. Vertical title, tappable, lifts on press.
components.css: .ds-spine { width: 28px; height: 108px; background: #2F6FB0; border: 2px solid #2B1D14; border-radius: 3px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; overflow: hidden; transition: transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-spine:hover { transform: translateY(-8px); } .ds-spine__title { writing-mode: vertical-rl; transform: rotate(180deg); font-family: 'Figtree', sans-serif; font-weight: 900; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 0.6px; color: #FFFFFF; white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
Booklistd is a hand-painted bookcase, not a cover grid. Every copy a reader owns renders as its own standing spine — colored, outlined, sized and patterned deterministically from the copy's database id, so the same book always wears the same spine. Shelves are rooms; a plank of color carries a room tag pill and a handwritten tape note. Dewey, a small SVG bookworm, sits on one shelf and says one true, dry, data-driven thing about the library — never about the owner. The whole world runs on six fixed inks plus paper, 2–2.5px outlines, and hard offset shadows with no blur; nothing is a tint, a gradient, or a soft glow. This is Operate register (PRODUCT.md): the redesign's charm lives in precise, reliable details — the Store Mode verdict, the pocket card, the shelf props — never at the expense of scan speed or legibility.

The build replaces "Reading nook at golden hour" (cream + Fraunces + clay + soft warm shadows) outright. Nothing from that world survives except the underlying data model; palette, type, shadow language and signature components are new from the ground up.
keyCharacteristics: Six fixed inks (tomato, bus/yellow, pool, grass, plum, tape) plus paper and brown ink — no tints, no gradients, halftone dots for extra tone
Every shape carries a 2–2.5px ink outline and a hard 3–4px offset shadow (never soft, never blurred)
Bagel Fat One for display type, Figtree for all UI, Gochi Hand reserved for handwritten asides
Yellow (bus) is spoken for: it is the primary-action color and nothing else
Each owned copy's spine is deterministic and permanent, derived from its row id
Dewey's lines are generated from real counts — never invented, never aimed at the reader

rules.name: The Yellow Rule
rules.body: bus (#F4B41A) is the primary-action color and nothing else: the Scan sticker, primary buttons, and Store Mode's own chrome (viewfinder, scan line, session pill). No decorative, informational or secondary use anywhere in the app.

rules.name: The No-Tint Rule
rules.body: Every color in the system is one of the fixed inks at full saturation, or paper/white. Extra visual weight comes from a halftone dot pattern, an outline weight change, or a different ink — never from lightening, darkening or fading a color toward transparency.

rules.name: The Controls-Never-Handwrite Rule
rules.body: Gochi Hand renders only inside TapeNote. Every pressable — buttons, chips, tabs, stamps, stickers — uses Figtree, never the hand font, so nothing a user must tap is rendered in a script face.

rules.name: The Raised Rule
rules.body: Depth is always a solid offset shape behind the content, drawn at the shape's own outline color, never a translucent/blurred shadow. If it isn't drawn by Raised, it isn't a shadow in this system.

dos: Do keep bus yellow exclusive to primary actions and Store Mode's own chrome (the Yellow Rule).
Do draw all depth as a solid offset shape via Raised, never a blurred/translucent shadow.
Do derive a copy's spine and fallback cover deterministically from its id, so it never changes between sessions.
Do keep secondary text warm-toned (soft #6B5646 light / #D9C3A0 lamp) — never true gray.
Do keep Dewey's lines true and data-driven (built from real counts/loans/wishlist age), roasting the library, never the reader.
Do silence Dewey on errors, permission prompts and destructive confirmations; those use plain librarian copy that names the problem and the fix.
Do cap Dewey's lines at 70 characters and hide them entirely (bubbles, tape-note jokes, toast quips) under the Quiet librarian setting.
Do collapse the verdict stamp/sticker/Dewey-pop sequence to static, non-scaling end states under reduced motion, while keeping verdict color, copy and haptics.
donts: Don't introduce a tint, gradient, or lightened/darkened variant of an ink — reach for a different ink or a halftone dot pattern instead.
Don't give a shape a soft or blurred shadow, an ambient glow, or native elevation — every raised surface in this world uses the hard-offset Raised layer.
Don't render Gochi Hand on anything pressable; it is reserved for TapeNote alone.
Don't invent a Dewey line — every line must trace to a real count, duplicate, loan, or wishlist-age value in the context object it's built from.
Don't use emoji as icons or status markers; the app's only iconography is inline SVG line art (back chevron, close X) or the illustrated components above.
Don't stack cards inside cards, or build a metric-grid of big-number tiles; use PocketCard + LeaderRow's dotted-leader rows instead.

Don't place an eyebrow/kicker label over a display headline as a new pattern — the build carries exactly one instance of this (the Shelves greeting over "Booklistd"), and it is a defect this DESIGN.md does not extend into a system rule.
